key_concepts: Bone COMP is the object component used to build bone chains for character rigs and IK-driven deformation workflows.
A child Bone COMP attaches to the end of its parent bone, while a bone parented under a non-bone component attaches to that component origin.
Xform controls define the bone object transform, while kinematic range, damping, and rolloff parameters constrain IK motion.
Capture controls and display-capture geometry define the region used by capture/deform workflows.
Bone Creation state is the intended workflow for end-to-end chains; internal SOP networks can customize link and capture-region geometry.
common_gotchas: Bone children attach to the end of the parent bone, not the parent's origin.
Use the Bone Creation state for chains; manual operator-by-operator placement is slow and often produces worse-behaved rigs.
Bones do not render by default; link geometry and capture region geometry are display/capture aids.
Standard Capture/Deform setups use IK CHOP expressions in transform channels, so direct manual edits may be overridden.
A bone parented under a non-bone component attaches to that component's origin unless translate expressions are removed.
Capture regions are generated by internal SOPs and can be customized by editing the Bone COMP's SOP network.
build_relevance: 2021.10000+ character rigging, IK, and capture regions
